supportingEvidence.title: Reuters: Iran sets conditions for reopening Strait of Hormuz
supportingEvidence.note: Reuters reports Mohsen Rezaei saying Iran is formulating conditions for reopening Hormuz, including ending the regional war, lifting what Iran calls the blockade of its ports, compensation for losses and sanctions relief.

supportingEvidence.title: Qatar Ministry of Foreign Affairs: Qatar PM meets Iran Supreme National Security Council secretary
supportingEvidence.note: Primary Qatari source confirms the meeting with Mohsen Rezaei focused on regional escalation and de-escalation efforts, independently confirming the negotiating channel but not the specific Iranian conditions.

supportingEvidence.title: Qatar Ministry of Foreign Affairs: interim Hormuz corridor and mine-clearing framework remains under discussion
supportingEvidence.note: Primary Qatari source confirms ongoing discussion of a temporary joint shipping corridor and mine-clearing project, not a finalized unconditional reopening.

contradictingEvidence.title: Qatar readout does not confirm Iran's reported reopening demands as agreed terms
contradictingEvidence.note: Qatar's primary readout describes an interim corridor and mine-clearing framework but does not say the U.S. accepted Iran's reported conditions or that a final reopening agreement exists.

contradictingEvidence.title: Reuters: shipping traffic has risen slightly despite unresolved standoff
contradictingEvidence.note: Physical traffic is showing some improvement even without a final political settlement, so passage may recover incrementally before the full reported Iranian demand set is resolved.

falsifier: Downgrade the conditional-reopening thesis if Iran or a controlling primary source retracts or materially narrows the reported conditions, if the U.S./Iran/Oman/Qatar publish an unconditional operational reopening framework, or if sustained commercial traffic and downstream deliveries normalize without the reported conditions being met.

title: Iran shifts Hormuz reopening from mediation-only to explicit conditionality
summary: Iran is now reportedly formulating explicit conditions for reopening Hormuz, while Qatar's primary readouts confirm an active interim corridor and mine-clearing negotiation channel but do not confirm those demands as accepted or a final agreement. The state is therefore CONDITIONAL_REOPENING_DEMANDS + MEDIATION_ACTIVE, not NORMALIZING.
delta: Supersede the simpler MEDIATION_ACTIVE + DIRECT_TALKS_ABSENT state with CONDITIONAL_REOPENING_DEMANDS + MEDIATION_ACTIVE + FRAMEWORK_UNRESOLVED. Preserve prior traffic-recovery evidence separately: incremental physical passage can improve even while the political conditions remain unresolved.
firstOrderImpacts: lower probability of an immediate unconditional Hormuz normalization
continued oil, freight and insurance sensitivity to whether Iranian conditions are narrowed or accepted
higher value of separating mediator activity from negotiated terms and operational passage
secondOrderImpacts: market pricing may oscillate as each condition is treated as independently negotiable rather than as a binary peace/no-peace state
commercial shipping can partially recover before political settlement, creating a divergence between legal-political state and physical flow
Orbital Insight should track demand-set evolution, mediator confirmation and physical throughput as separate state variables

alphaHunter.hypothesis: A structured conditionality graph that tracks which Iranian reopening demands are accepted, rejected or bypassed will classify Hormuz normalization earlier and more accurately than generic 'talks progressing' headlines or crude-price reaction alone.
alphaHunter.baseline: headline sentiment about mediation/reopening plus Brent/WTI reaction
alphaHunter.alternativeData: condition-by-condition diplomatic state, Qatar/Oman primary readouts, vessel throughput, war-risk insurance, freight, maritime incidents and downstream import arrivals
alphaHunter.incrementalValueMetric: 3-7 day classification accuracy and lead time for PARTIAL_PASSAGE / CONDITIONAL_REOPENING / NORMALIZING versus the simple headline-price baseline
alphaHunter.killCondition: Kill the conditionality layer if physical traffic and downstream deliveries normalize independently of the reported conditions or if condition tracking does not improve held-out state classification versus public headlines and price.
